description:
FILED s543j (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22) from #5001's probe list.  Before s543j both were SILENT (lowered as a plain delete, the element gone for good); s543j's #5001 fix sends every expression-position `delete local` through the #3370 hoist, whose CHECKED precondition (ir-spec 7.2 "A `local` TERM") refuses these two: a binary operator before the term is not on the inert list, and the first `delete $h{a}` is a call that runs BEFORE the second term and names the same hash.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s543j/probes/file in the s543j worktree (agent-abcd8b98eb856dbee)/t5330.pl):
    our %h = (a => 'A', b => 'B', k => 'K');
    sub f { my @v = (delete local $h{a}, delete local $h{b}); "@v|" . join(",", sort keys %h) } print f(), "|", join(",", sort keys %h), "\n";
    sub g { 1 + delete local $h{k}; exists $h{k} ? "E" : "N" } print g(), $h{k}, "\n";
  perl: A B|k|a,b,k / NK      PCL (s543j): PCL: refused statement ... (#3370)      PCL (main b58114ca): A B|k|k / N (silent)

DIRECTION: widen _token_inert_before_local to the value operators that apply AFTER both operands (+ - * / . x == eq ... -- never && || // ?: and or, which decide whether the term runs) and let a `delete`-of-a-different-key word count as inert when its operand names no key the term's operand names (static keys only) -- a ruled precondition (s519 #1), so a widening needs the gate-set scan.

=== s543j review round (22:3x) ===
More positions now land on this refusal (they were SILENT plain deletes through the seam or the plain delete before s543j): a ternary arm (`my $t = C ? delete local $h{b} : 0`, and as a void statement), an `&&` / `||` / `//` operand, `($x, $y) = (delete local $h{b}, 5)` (the LHS list's comma before the term), a hash-constructor value `{ k => delete local $h{b} }` (the `=>` before the term).  Reproducers the s543j worktree (agent-abcd8b98eb856dbee) scratch/s543j/probes/m1r (r01-r04, r07-r09).  The same widening shape covers them: an element separator inside a Constructor / an assignment's LHS list is inert; a ternary / short-circuit arm needs a CONDITIONAL hoist (`my $c = !!C; my $t = $c ? ELEM : undef; local ELEM = $t if $c; ... ($c ? delete ELEM : ...)`) -- not attempted.


=== DONE (s543l) for family (i); (ii) MEASURED, NOT FIXED (s543l) ===
(i) FIXED.  The #3370 hoist's CHECKED precondition (Parser2::_hoist_local_term) takes three more facts, each a
position where nothing evaluated before the term can observe it, and only OUTSIDE a deref block (a scope of its own in
perl: #5381 filed for the old first-term hoist there):
  * a VALUE operator (+ - * / % ** x . & | ^ << >> == != <=> < > <= >= eq ne lt gt le ge cmp) applies after both
    operands -- _value_operator (never && || // ?: .. or an assignment operator);
  * a comma / `=>` NESTED in a parenthesised list or a constructor separates elements -- _nested_element_comma (an
    assignment's left list, a constructor value, a list's earlier element);
  * a `delete` of ANOTHER literal key of the term's own aggregate -- _other_key_delete / _static_key.
The tokens before the term are still asked one by one, so the breaking shapes stay the refusal: `$h{k} . delete local
$h{k}`, `r() . delete local $h{k}` (r reads %h), `id($h{k}) . delete local $h{k}`; and, conservatively, a read of
ANOTHER element before the term (`$h{a} . delete local $h{k}`) and two deletes of the SAME key.  Probes
scratch/s543l/probes/m5 (in the s543l worktree): 15 shapes, base 0 -> tree 8 = perl (f01 f02 f03 f04 f05 f12 f14 f15);
the 7 left are the refusal (f06 ternary, f07 &&, f08-f11, f13).  A side effect, perl's answer: `(my $x, local $_) =
@_` (ExtUtils::CBuilder Windows.pm, dumpvar.pl) is now hoisted and restored -- it was announced 'not localized'
(local-term-01.t 7h; 7g moved to `(h()->{x}, local $_) = @_`, which the hoist still refuses).  Guard local-elem-02.t N4.

(ii) NOT FIXED -- a ternary arm / an `&&` / `||` / `//` operand.  The term may not run, so its save must be GATED on
the operand's condition, evaluated ONCE: p-local-maybe expresses the gate, but the statement itself must then read
the condition's TEMPORARY in place of the condition (`my $t = C ? delete local $h{b} : 0` ->
  my $c = !!(C); my $old = $c ? $h{b} : undef; local $h{b} = $old if $c; my $t = $c ? delete $h{b} : 0;
`A && delete local E` -> `my $c = A; ...; $c && delete E` with $c holding A's VALUE, not !!A, since `&&` yields it).
That is a rewrite of the statement's text at the condition's tokens -- a new hoist kind beside the leading-term and
the modifier ones, not the existing gate (the brief's line).  Design sketch: _hoist_local_term learns a CONDITIONAL
owner -- the nearest enclosing `?:` / `&&` / `||` / `//` whose RIGHT operand holds the term; the tokens of its left
operand must pass the inert test (they run first); the rebuilt statement replaces exactly those tokens by `$c`
(for `||`: the local is gated on !$c, for `//`: on !defined $c).  Left refused: tidy and loud (PCL: refused statement
... (#3370)).


FINAL SHA (s543l, 2026-11-27): the batch is MERGE-READY at 2f85209e, rebased onto main 4b0d5d50 (its code = s543m final 5d426786 + this batch; the review fix L1 for #5333 is 6a1301ed); the notes above cite pre-rebase shas.
subject: LOUD: a `delete local` term after a binary operator (`1 + delete local $h{k}`) or after an earlier call on the same aggregate (`(delete local $h{a}, delete local $h{b})`) is refused -- "local in this expression position is not supported (#3370)"
triage_reason: a delete local term the #3370 hoist precondition refuses (LOUD)
